clue.text: Number on University Challenge team notice one's slept in

parts.note: each side on the TV quiz University Challenge has four players
a poster is a notice put up on a wall

explanation.surface: A quiz-team member reads a notice about the TV contest University Challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: University Challenge is a long-running British TV quiz in which teams of four students compete.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed with a post at each corner is something a person sleeps in.

clue.text: Juliet visiting France, Italy, India and another country

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so this letter is put inside the others

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Juliet tours several European countries and India, then yet another nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific island nation is simply one more country after those listed.

clue.text: Row after meeting of countries leads to release

indicators.note: the row comes after the meeting, so its letters follow

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations, an assembly of countries
a chain is a row or series of linked things

explanation.surface: An argument following a summit of nations ends in someone being freed.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from shackles is to release them.

clue.text: Bar very piercing clarinets, playing as one in the town hall?

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: one thing piercing another goes into it, so this letter goes inside
the clarinets being played means the word's letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: In a bar, very shrill clarinets are played by someone acting the part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piercing' puts V inside LICSERANT, the anagram of CLARINETS signalled by 'playing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Council officials working in a municipal building are an example of state employees, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Film outline in which arsenic wrecked love

indicators.note: the word arsenic is wrecked, its letters smashed into a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A screenplay plot in which poison ruins a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay's summary of plot and scenes is called by this term.

clue.text: Something for the mind that's offered in a tablet?

definitions.text: Something for the mind that's offered in a tablet?

parts.words: Something for the mind that's offered in a tablet?
parts.note: suggests a pill or medicine for mental health, but means reading matter delivered on a tablet computer

explanation.definitionFit: A digital book read on a handheld device feeds the mind and comes on a tablet.

clue.text: Long gradient with no parking

indicators.note: with no parking means that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: the pitch of a roof is its slope or gradient
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A long steep hill where you cannot park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the slope; it is a verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn for something is to have a craving or desire, a verb sense.

clue.text: Twirl in tango with violin, losing head

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped from the word for violin

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: Spinning around while dancing a tango with a violin, and falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes F from FIDDLE, leaving IDDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle with or twist something idly between the fingers is to twirl it.

clue.text: Cast-off worker sad to receive note

indicators.note: the pair of words receive the note between them

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
down means sad
me (also mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A depressed labourer gets a message.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing passed on from an older sibling is a discarded garment.

clue.text: Patriarch's account in prophetic book

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the book's name

parts.note: Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An Old Testament father figure's story appears in a book of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac's son is one of the three Hebrew patriarchs of Genesis.

clue.text: Affection's gone west — moving out in progress

indicators.note: in an across clue going west is right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: love is affection

indicators.note: the words out in are moving, their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Love has died as someone moves out in the middle of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone west' gives EVOL, and 'moving' turns OUT IN into UTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual development over time is progress in the sense of advancement.

clue.text: In clues, yearns to be funny, superfluously

indicators.note: the letters are made funny, that is odd or askew, and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter longs to make clues amusing, though this is overdoing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without need is doing it in excess, beyond what is required.

clue.text: The French bird over country seeing all the wildlife

indicators.note: turned over, these letters are read backwards

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
the mina (also myna) is an Asian starling
a kingdom is a country ruled by a monarch

explanation.surface: A French bird flies over a country and spots every kind of creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The taxonomic grouping of all creatures covers every living beast.

clue.text: Moist sea creatures British caught, not Germany — they won't go off

parts.note: damp means moist

indicators.note: the letter is caught inside the shortened word
not Germany means that letter is removed

parts.note: squids are sea creatures
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Wet sea creatures are landed by British fishermen but not German ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes D from SQUIDS, leaving SQUIS, and 'caught' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet fireworks fail to explode, and figuratively these are disappointing anticlimaxes.

clue.text: One questioning what's in mailbag — no stickers?

indicators.note: what's in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about the contents of a mailbag with no stamps on the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who doubts whether a god exists is a religious questioner.

clue.text: Long dull passage covered in loose rock, apparently

definitions.meaning: a lengthy tedious piece of writing
a whimsical sense: as if scree, loose mountain stones, had been spread over it

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition invents a word: 'apparently' admits it reads as scree plus a past-tense ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tiresome piece of writing or speech is the standard sense.

clue.text: Leo, maybe journalist, definitely not up to be recruited

parts.note: Leo is an example of a sign of the zodiac
ED is short for editor, a journalist

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read backwards

parts.note: no means definitely not

explanation.surface: A Leo who works as a journalist is certainly not keen on joining up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining up formally, by putting your name to papers, means being enlisted.

clue.text: Modern work — revolutionary work with character

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a part is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: A contemporary piece of art described as radical and full of character.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s movement of Warhol and Lichtenstein produced modern artworks.

clue.text: Computer aid for good memory

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
RAM is random-access memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A tool to help remember things on a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Software, spelt this way in computing, is what tells a machine what to do.

clue.text: Propeller engineer carries west

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A ship's propeller is fitted by an engineer heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' looks like a noun; it is a verb rearranging CARRIES plus W.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's propeller is the rotating blade unit, in older terminology.

clue.text: Revolutionise karaoke to collect rising gains

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up, backwards
the words collect the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone transforms karaoke in order to bring in increasing profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to collect' picks NISEKAR from inside the two words, and 'rising' reverses it. 'Revolutionise' looks like an anagram signal but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Accumulating money in large amounts is a phrasal verb for earning or gaining.

clue.text: One starts a speech that another puts a stop to

definitions.text: One starts a speech that another puts a stop to

parts.words: One starts a speech that another puts a stop to
parts.note: sounds like a heckler interrupting an orator, but describes the opening and closing punctuation around reported speech

explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas open direct speech, and a matching one closes it.

clue.text: Bury theatrical writer misses opening

indicators.note: the first letter of the name is missed out

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British playwright

explanation.surface: A dramatist fails to attend the premiere of his play in a town called Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town name; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a body in the ground is a verb sense of burial.

clue.text: Bargain brooches sent to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: pins are brooches

explanation.surface: Cheap brooches are dispatched to northern customers.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang something cheap at the price is a real steal.

clue.text: I had to restrain rattier drunk becoming angry

indicators.note: the outer letters hold in, restrain, the others

parts.note: I'd is short for I had

indicators.note: the word rattier is drunk, its letters staggered

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hold back a tipsy, more irritable companion who is getting cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' and 'to restrain' both look like surface story about a drinker being held back; 'becoming' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being annoyed or riled is close to being cross.

clue.text: Playwright in limbo, seeing odd characters cut

indicators.note: removing the odd-numbered letters leaves the alternate even ones

explanation.surface: A dramatist in limbo watches eccentric people being edited out.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd characters looks like strange people; it means letters 1, 3, 5 and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik, the Norwegian dramatist of A Doll's House, was a playwright.

clue.text: Part or whole read aloud

indicators.note: the word is said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a sum is a whole, a total

explanation.surface: A text is read out in part or in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion of a quantity, as in 'have a portion', is a fraction of it.

clue.text: Biscuit trademark with flower rejected

parts.note: a brand is a trademark

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a pansy is a flower

explanation.surface: A cookie brand has its flower logo turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin crisp rolled ginger wafer is a classic British sweet biscuit.
